text:
devon: Heads-up — saw a cluster-wide bump in nv_gpu_xid_count + ECC spikes in eu-west1 around 02:13 UTC. DCGM exporter shows short-lived bursts on 3 racks, not steady.

morgan: which metric exactly? XID codes or the ECC counter?

devon: both. nv_gpu_ecc_errors_total increased in small bursts, and nv_gpu_xid_errors has matching short spikes. pattern: ~3–5 spikes over 10m on the same card UID, then quiet.

priya: can you paste the PromQL you used?

devon: pulled this quickly from grafana: 
```
sum by(card_uuid) (increase(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]))
```
and a correlate join with ECC: 
```
sum by(card_uuid) (increase(nv_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))
```
But need a way to coalesce transient bursts and avoid pager noise.

samir: agree. we should score short bursts differently than sustained growth. thinking an anomaly score rule combining: XID spikes, ECC spikes, and recent gpu_temp high tail. weight them and only alert when score > threshold for >15m.

priya: +1. Also we should avoid high-cardinality alerts. label by card_uuid is ok but we must limit to cards that are in prod pools (annotation from node exporter/pod). maybe use node label: gpu_pool=prod.

devon: prototype rule I threw together: 
```
# recording: per-card 5m increases
record: infra:gpu:xid_5m:sum
expr: sum by(card_uuid) (increase(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]))

record: infra:gpu:ecc_5m:sum
expr: sum by(card_uuid) (increase(nv_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))

record: infra:gpu:temp_95p
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le,card_uuid) (rate(nv_gpu_temperature_celsius_bucket[10m])))
```
Then alert rule: 
```
alert: GPUAnomalyScore
expr: (
  infra:gpu:xid_5m:sum * 3 +
  infra:gpu:ecc_5m:sum * 2 +
  (infra:gpu:temp_95p > 85) * 4
) > 5
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "gpu anomaly on {{ $labels.card_uuid }}"
  runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-anomaly"
```
Note: multipliers tuned ad-hoc. we can move to prometheus recording rules first and test with replay.

morgan: clever. two notes: (1) (infra:gpu:temp_95p > 85) yields 0/1 but you multiply by 4 which is fine. (2) For noise suppression, add a stable-hold with avg over 3 windows. maybe record moving average: infra:gpu:anomaly_avg = avg_over_time((score_expr)[30m]) and only fire if avg > threshold.

priya: Also we need to avoid alerts for nodes in draining state or scheduled for RMA. can we join node annotations? e.g. only fire when node_annotation != draining. label_replace can help.

samir: good catch. we have label on kube_node: node_maintenance=true for those nodes. add `unless on(card_uuid) kube_node_annotation_maintenance == 1`.

devon: will add an exclude: 
```
# in alert expr
and on(card_uuid) (kube_node_annotation_maintenance != "true")
```
but we need to confirm the exporter exposes card_uuid -> node mapping.

infra-bot: automated note: I replayed 72h of metrics for eu-west1 with the proposed recording rules and threshold=5. Results: 27 candidate cards, 9 would have paged (with 15m for>), of those 9, 6 correspond to cards that later had driver resets within 24h. FP rate ~33%.

morgan: that's promising. what's the 33% FPR definition? which were false positives?

infra-bot: false positives here = cards that matched score>threshold but had no subsequent ECC/XID escalation or RMA within 7d. We trimmed maintenance and drain labels.

priya: ok next steps: 1) land recording rules only (no alert) in a staging ruleset; 2) run 7d backfill replay, produce weekly report with TP/FP; 3) iterate weights and the hold window.

devon: I'll open a PR with the recording rules and a test harness to replay metrics. also adding an exporter-side metric to expose pci_reset_count if kernel reports it (nvml/pci resets) — that helped explain some bursts historically.

samir: can you also add a PromQL snippet to aggregate by rack label so SRE can target a rack-level sweep before paging? e.g. `sum by(rack) (infra:gpu:xid_5m:sum)`.

devon: yep. I'll include that and a quick grafana panel so on-call can triage rack vs card.

morgan: bot action items: PR link, test output, and a proposed tuning doc. aim for low-risk rollout: record rules -> observe 48h -> then alert in low-sev channel for a week -> then page if stable.

priya: +1. Also add a note about not firing for ephemeral bursts tied to large batch jobs. maybe add job label filtering: `unless (job =~ "batch-.*")` or reduce weight for pods with label `ephemeral=true`.

devon: thanks. I'll push the PR and add a small synthetic test where we inject an XID spike for 3m vs 20m to validate suppression logic.

samir: sounds good. tag me on the PR.

devon: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/I-2345 (recording rules + replay harness + grafana dashboard). please review. :thumbsup:

priya: reviewing now. looks solid. we should schedule a 30m sync after merging to eyeball real-time graphs when it rolls out to staging.

morgan: ping when staging rule is live. thanks all. :coffee:
